GEOGRAPHY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GEOGRAPHY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Measure rainfall only
   B. Name the president
   C. Replace the compass rose
   D. Explain symbols used on a map

2. Which statement about Climate is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Climate never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Climate as rumours only.
   C. Explain Climate with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Climate.

3. Which statement about Mass Wasting is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Mass Wasting with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Mass Wasting as rumours only.
   C. Say Mass Wasting never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Mass Wasting.

4. Which statement about Statistical Methods is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Statistical Methods.
   B. Treat Statistical Methods as rumours only.
   C. Say Statistical Methods never happens in Kenya.
   D. Explain Statistical Methods with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

5. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Littering in markets
   B. Obeying laws and caring for public property
   C. Destroying road signs
   D. Avoiding all community work

6. Which statement about Water Cycle and Action of Rivers is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Water Cycle and Action of Rivers never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Water Cycle and Action of Rivers as rumours only.
   C. Explain Water Cycle and Action of Rivers with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Water Cycle and Action of Rivers.

7. Which statement about Weather is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Weather as rumours only.
   B. Explain Weather with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Weather.
   D. Say Weather never happens in Kenya.

8. Which statement about Geographic Information Systems is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Geographic Information Systems with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Geographic Information Systems as rumours only.
   C. Say Geographic Information Systems never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Geographic Information Systems.

9. Which statement about Map Reading and Interpretation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Map Reading and Interpretation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Say Map Reading and Interpretation never happens in Kenya.
   C. Treat Map Reading and Interpretation as rumours only.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Map Reading and Interpretation.

10. Which statement about Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in never happens in Kenya.
   B. Explain Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in.
   D. Treat Agriculture - Wheat in Kenya and Russia - Maize in Kenya and Mexico, - Coffee in as rumours only.

11. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nairobi
   C. Nakuru
   D. Mombasa

12. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Ignore prices in shops
   B. Hide all money underground
   C. Plan income and spending wisely
   D. Avoid saving forever

13. Which statement about Vegetation is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Vegetation as rumours only.
   B. Explain Vegetation with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Skip evidence when discussing Vegetation.
   D. Say Vegetation never happens in Kenya.

14. Which statement about Elementary Surveying is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Elementary Surveying.
   B. Explain Elementary Surveying with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Say Elementary Surveying never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Elementary Surveying as rumours only.

15. Which statement about Soils is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Soils never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Soils.
   C. Explain Soils with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Treat Soils as rumours only.

16. Which statement about Weathering is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Weathering with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Weathering.
   C. Treat Weathering as rumours only.
   D. Say Weathering never happens in Kenya.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Elementary Surveying and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Statistical Methods and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Geographic Information Systems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Weather and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Climate and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Vegetation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Weathering and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Mass Wasting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Soils and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Water Cycle and Action of Rivers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
